title: D-Wave and Nasdaq Verafin Partner to Develop Quantum Applications for Financial Crime Detection - Quantum Computing Report
gist: D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS) has signed Nasdaq Verafin — Nasdaq's financial crime unit serving 2,800+ institutions with roughly $13 trillion in collective assets — to a proof-of-concept applying quantum annealing and quantum machine learning via the Leap cloud to AML, fraud, and scam detection. The strategic wager is that annealing plus graph analysis delivers testable commercial value on messy counterparty-network data years ahead of fault-tolerant gate machines.

themes.theme: Distribution reach of the Verafin channel

insights.claim: Nasdaq Verafin provides financial crime management solutions to more than 2,800 financial institutions representing approximately $13 trillion in collective assets, making it one of the largest single distribution channels any quantum vendor has secured.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: If the PoC converts, D-Wave gets embedded distribution to thousands of banks without selling a single machine — the highest-leverage commercialization path in the sector.
insights.quote: Nasdaq Verafin provides financial crime management solutions to more than 2,800 financial institutions representing approximately $13 trillion in collective assets.
insights.locator: If successful, the initial PoC will lay the foundation

insights.claim: Success in the PoC is explicitly intended to expand into pilot applications integrated directly into Nasdaq Verafin's commercial anti-financial-crime software suite, meaning the end state is quantum embedded inside a shipping enterprise product rather than sold as compute time.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Embedded-in-product is a recurring-revenue model with far better economics than per-hour cloud access; watch for a stated integration milestone as the value inflection.
insights.locator: If successful, the initial PoC will lay the foundation

insights.claim: The counterparty is the financial crime technology unit of Nasdaq itself, giving the engagement an exchange-operator imprimatur that carries weight with bank compliance buyers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Compliance software procurement is reference-driven; a Nasdaq-branded quantum pilot de-risks the category for every follower institution.
insights.locator: Nasdaq Verafin-the financial crime management technology unit of Nasdaq

themes.theme: Technical approach: annealing on counterparty graphs

insights.claim: Nasdaq Verafin will use D-Wave's quantum annealing hardware via the Leap quantum cloud service to examine hundreds of potential data signals simultaneously across account activity, transaction histories, and multi-entity counterparty networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Access is cloud-delivered, so revenue flows through Leap consumption — a metric to track in D-Wave's bookings rather than system sales.
insights.quote: examine hundreds of potential data signals simultaneously across account activity, transaction histories, and multi-entity counterparty networks
insights.locator: Nasdaq Verafin will utilize D-Wave's quantum annealing hardware

insights.claim: The method maps multi-dimensional network features into combinatorial optimization and quantum machine learning models to surface hidden behavioral patterns and anomalous fraud signals that conventional classical monitoring tools may overlook.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Recasting fraud detection as feature selection over a combinatorial space is the reusable pattern; the same mapping applies to credit risk and insurance fraud.
insights.quote: uncover hidden behavioral patterns and anomalous fraud signals that conventional classical monitoring tools may overlook
insights.locator: By mapping these multi-dimensional network features

insights.claim: The PoC is scoped specifically to evaluate how quantum-hybrid algorithms analyze complex, non-linear data relationships, an honest framing that the technical question is still open rather than settled.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Evaluation language, not deployment language — do not model revenue from this agreement until pilot integration is announced.
insights.quote: The partnership will begin with a proof-of-concept (PoC) project designed to evaluate how quantum-hybrid algorithms analyze complex, non-linear data relationships.
insights.locator: The partnership will begin with a proof-of-concept

insights.claim: The workflow splits into multi-signal data ingestion on the classical side and QML feature selection plus combinatorial optimization on the annealer, meaning the quantum component is a narrow accelerator inside a mostly classical pipeline.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Narrow-accelerator architectures are the realistic near-term quantum business model; the classical pipeline, not the qubits, determines whether it ships.

themes.theme: Annealing as a pre-fault-tolerance commercial wedge

insights.claim: Leadership from both firms argue that applying quantum annealing to graph analysis and machine learning gives financial institutions a practical framework for testing real-world quantum advantages ahead of fault-tolerant systems.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This is the core bull case for annealing-levered names: revenue in the gap years before FTQC, which gate-based competitors cannot address.
insights.quote: applying quantum annealing to graph analysis and machine learning provides financial institutions with a practical framework for testing real-world quantum advantages ahead of fault-tolerant systems
insights.locator: Leadership from D-Wave and Nasdaq Verafin noted

insights.claim: Positioning annealing as useful today implicitly concedes that fault-tolerant gate-based machines remain far enough out that a bridge technology has a viable commercial window.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The bridge-technology framing is also its risk: the window closes if FTQC timelines compress, so annealing exposure is a duration-sensitive trade.

insights.claim: The agreement is described as another commercial deployment for D-Wave's dual-platform strategy, following a recent network operations expansion with AT&T, indicating a repeatable pattern of landing large enterprise anchor customers in regulated industries.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Two anchor logos in telecom and financial compliance suggest a sales motion that is starting to compound; track the cadence of new named enterprise deals as the key QBTS operating metric.
insights.quote: The agreement marks another commercial deployment for D-Wave’s dual-platform strategy, following its recent network operations expansion with AT&T.
insights.locator: The agreement marks another commercial deployment

insights.claim: Targeting anti-money-laundering, fraud detection, and scam prevention aims quantum at a workload where regulatory mandate — not ROI discretion — forces banks to keep spending, insulating budgets from IT cost cycles.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Compliance-mandated budgets are the most defensible place to introduce an unproven technology; expect other quantum vendors to copy this vertical choice.
insights.locator: enhance predictive modeling for anti-money laundering (AML)
